articleTitle: Design of a self regulated flash type ADC with high resolution
abstract: The paper presents a unique design based on flash type ADCs having a high resolution. A novel cyclic architecture concept has been proposed for its implementation. The most important feature of this ADC is that two reference voltages are employed along with flash ADC logic. An 8 bit conventional flash type ADC requires 255 comparators for its implementation. Following this, a 4 bit flash type ADC requires 15 comparators. But the proposed model employs only three comparators to realize an 8 bit resolution in only four clock cycles. The design is verified in hardware and also simulated in MATLAB SIMULINK software. Relative advantages and disadvantages are discussed with respect to the conventional flash and SAR type ADCs.

articleTitle: Comparative performance analysis of various tuning methods in the design of PID controller
abstract: In this paper, the performance of different tuning methods of PID controller is evaluated. Tuning of PID controller parameters is necessary due to the wide applications of controllers in industry. Different tuning methods such as Empirical Ziegler-Nichols, Cohen-Coon, Chien-Hrones-Reswick and optimum tuning methods are considered. The performance of the above mentioned tuning methods are evaluated on the feedback control problem which controls the outlet temperature of heat exchanger system. Set point regulation and load disturbance rejection property of the controller are evaluated. The simulation results exhibit low overshoot and low settling time for most of the tuning rules. A comparative evaluation of the performance is carried out.

articleTitle: Blending Roulette wheel selection with Simulated Annealing for Job Shop Scheduling problem
abstract: The Job Shop Scheduling Problem (known as JSSP) is a wellknown and one of the difficult combinatorial optimization problems and treated as a member of NP-complete problem class. This paper presents an algorithm based on Simulated Annealing method to solve the Job Shop Scheduling problem. It is an approximation algorithm for finding the minimum makespan in a job shop. The proposed algorithm is based on Roulette wheel selection and simulated annealing, a generalization of the well known and effective iterative improvement approach for combinatorial optimization problems. The generalization involves the acceptance of cost-increasing transitions with a nonzero probability to avoid getting stuck in local minima. The problem studied in this research focuses on the sequencing of operations and allocation of operation to the machine under some sequence constraint.

articleTitle: A quality prediction method for weight lifting activity
abstract: Activity recognition has found immense interest in the field of sports activity recognition in recent time. The application has found extensive utility in giving machine based feedback on how well the performance in training is by any sports athlete. The present work proposes a model to predict the quality of training along with the mistakes which can have a severe effect on performance of the athlete or health condition of any subject. The dataset contains data of perfect execution of weight lifting activity and the same with four common mistakes. 34 features have been selected and used to train and test the proposed model. A multi-layer feed-forward network (MLP-FFN), RBFNN, Random Forest and Hidden Naïve Bayes (HNB) classifiers are employed to determine the objective. The assessment of used methods has been done by observing different performance measures such as Kappa statistic, Mean absolute error (MAE), Root mean squared error (RMSE), Relative absolute error (RAE), True positive (TP) Rate, False positive (FP) Rate and F-Measure. The experimental results have shown almost perfect classification using MLP-FFN and satisfactory results for all the proposed models.

articleTitle: Drive strategies for switched reluctance motor - A review
abstract: A typical switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive system is made up of three basic components: power electronic converter, control logic circuit and the switched reluctance motor. The principle of operation of a SRM motor is quite simple: as current passes through one of its stator windings, torque is produced by the tendency of its rotor to align with the excited stator pole. The direction of the torque generated is a function of rotor position with respect to the phase that is energized, and is independent of direction of flow of current in that specific winding. The torque production can be made continuous by synchronizing the excitation of each phase winding with rotor position. The amount of current passing through the SRM winding is controlled by suitably making the power electronic switches on and off, which can connect each SRM phase to the DC bus. The drive strategy of a SRM motor predominantly consists of the power electronic drive topology because it largely dictates how the motor can be used. This paper presents different drive techniques for a SRM motor collected from researches of a number of technologists.

articleTitle: Extraction of respiration signal from ECG for respiratory rate estimation
abstract: The necessity of respiratory monitoring is rapidly increasing in medical field to diagnose various cardio-pulmonary diseases. It is difficult to monitor respiration for ambulatory and ICU patients, as conventional methods are either obtrusive or suffer from low accuracy. The extraction of ECG derived respiration (EDR) signal using single-lead ECG has been proposed lately. This allows monitoring of ECG and respiration signal simultaneously from a recorded ECG signal. Recently few methods for EDR extraction from ECG are reported in literature. In this work, respiratory rates (RR) are derived from Heart Rate Variability (HRV) and Peak Amplitude Variation (PAV) method and a comparative study of these two methods is reported. Moreover, the validation of the proposed methods is made by comparing the obtained RR with that derived from original respiration signal. Subjects from Fantasia database and real-time data for both normal and with pulmonary diseases are considered for the work.

articleTitle: Detection of fault in a hybrid power system using wavelet transform
abstract: Proper detection of different kinds of faults appearing in a power system is extremely important. In this paper, detection and categorization of some of these faults are evaluated depending on the data obtained by the wavelet analysis of system transients. The energy of the signals detects the fault and threshold detail coefficient categorizes the fault into different types such as L-G, L-L-G, L-L-L. This paper finds how wavelet transform can detect and classify some abnormal conditions. The diagnostic technique suggested depends on the stationary wavelet transform.

articleTitle: Application of LVQ network in fault diagnosis of wind turbine using TurbSim, FAST and Simulink
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent diagnosis technique for wind turbine imbalance fault identification based on generator current signals. For this aim, Learning Vector Quantization (LVQ) Neural Network, which is powerful algorithm for classification problems that needs small complexity in solving nonlinear problems and applicable to high dimension applications, is employed. The complete dynamics of a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based wind-turbine (WTG) model are imitated in an amalgamated domain of Simulink, FAST and TurbSim under six distinct conditions, i.e., aerodynamic asymmetry, rotor furl imbalance, tail furl imbalance, blade imbalance, nacelle-yaw imbalance and normal operating scenarios. The simulation results in time domain of the PMSG stator current are decomposed into the Intrinsic Mode Frequency (IMF) using EMD method, which are utilized as input variable in LVQ. The analyzed results proclaim the effectiveness of the proposed approach to identify the healthy condition from imbalance faults in WTG. The presented work renders initial results that are helpful for online condition monitoring and health assessment of WTG.

articleTitle: A comparison between MPC and optimal PID controllers: Case studies
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study between the performance of Model Predictive Control (MPC) and optimal PID controllers in terms of various performance measures. Parameters of the PID controller are adjusted based on Bacterial Foraging Optimization (BFO) algorithm and its results are compared with those obtained using MPC controller in terms of some control parameters. These control parameters are rise time, settling time, peak overshoot percentage, integral of absolute errors and integral of time multiplied absolute of error for both MPC and PID controllers. Many case studies are considered in this article. First, second, third, fourth and fifth order systems are investigated. Simulation results indicate that MPC controller outperforms optimal PID controller in all cases.

Author Keywords: Bacterial Foraging Optimization and Performance Indices

articleTitle: Performance analysis of slip power recovery scheme employing two inverter topologies
abstract: This paper presents an approach for performance analysis of an induction motor utilizing the characteristics of slip power recovery schemes (SPRS). The performance is analyzed by using a three phase bridge recovery inverter without chopper and inverter with chopper. The simulation test for a 5.4 hp wound rotor induction motor is carried out on MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. The results of simulation are studied, analyzed and compared. It has been observed from the simulation results that the power factor and efficiency of the slip power recovery scheme using inverter with chopper has better values than the slip power recovery scheme using inverter without chopper.

articleTitle: Gravitational Search Algorithm based optimal Type-II controller for DC-DC Boost Converter
abstract: This paper proposes design and implementation of an optimal Type-II controller by using Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA) for obtaining better stability and performance of a closed loop DC-DC Switched Mode Boost Converter. Due to presence of a right-half-plane zero, boost converter suffers from non minimum phase problem in converter dynamics and it is difficult for the conventional PID controller to exhibit good performance with load, line variations and parametric uncertainty. GSA based optimal Type-II controller has been designed and simulations results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of optimized controllers for the converter.

articleTitle: Sequence operation theory based probabilistic load flow assessment with photovoltaic generation
abstract: This paper proposes a probabilistic load flow approach considering source and load uncertainties. Usually influence of these uncertainties is not considered in deterministic load flow. These uncertainties are a challenge to identify a competent and accurate method for load flow studies. Source uncertainty such as photovoltaic (PV) generation and load uncertainty are modelled as probabilistic discrete sequences and sequence operation theory is applied for load flow analysis. The disturbance in load flow pattern is studied in the presence of PV generation. Correctness of assuming a specific parametric distribution for real PV generation data is verified. DC load flow model is used to implement the proposed method to save memory and reduce computational time. Probabilistic distribution of output random variables (RVs) using proposed method and cumulant method are compared with the distributions obtained using Monte-Carlo simulation. The analysis is carried out on Wood and Woollenberg 6 bus system. The results have clearly established the fact that, application of the proposed method has accurately evaluated the distribution of output RVs.

articleTitle: Power network reconfiguration for congestion management and loss minimization using Genetic Algorithm
abstract: Network reconfiguration is referred as operational schemes to alter the network topology by closing and opening the sectionalizing and tie switches of power distribution system and thus it allows to control the power flow from substation to power consumers with additional benefits such as load balancing, real power loss reducing, optimizing the load sharing between parallel circuits by directing power flow along contractual paths. Restructuring of the power network, however, may increase the tendency of overloading and thus congestion in certain areas. This congestion may lead to violation of system voltage or transmission capacity limits and threaten the power network security and reliability. On this view point, this paper presents a Genetic Algorithm (GA) based new reconfiguration algorithm of the network which will able to identify the most congested area of power network and fabricate the least loss condition after alleviating overload and overvoltage as well as ensuring efficient network operation. To establish the efficacy of the proposed algorithm, case studies have been carried out on modified IEEE-14 bus and IEEE-30 bus power network and the results are found to be encouraging.

articleTitle: Design and development of contactless battery charger for underwater vehicles
abstract: Battery operated wireless sensor nodes, wireless network systems, autonomous underwater vehicles and underwater surveillance systems are in huge demand for maritime security and surveillance. Most of these systems are powered using rechargeable batteries. Recharging the batteries of these systems is considered as one of the challenges. In this paper, indigeneous design and development of contactless underwater battery charger is reported. The proposed system is designed using two approaches and their performances are compared and reported. The performance of 300W contactless underwater battery charger system designed is assessed under various test conditions and the results are reported. The proposed system can be easily adapted for various domestic applications too such as contactless pads to charge mobile phones, tablets, electric toothbrushes, electric shavers etc.

articleTitle: Calculation of power quality factor of supply system using labview
abstract: Monitoring of power supply is required in power systems to increase the performance, supervision and control over the system. Power quality is defined as perfectly sinusoidal voltage and uninterrupted power supply to the customers. The power quality factor (PQF) is a unique indicator ranging from 0 to 100%, which reflects quality of the 3 phase power supply given the user has been suggested here. Any industry or distribution system quality of supply and power consumption is accessed by Virtual instrumentation (VI). It monitors waveforms for variations in harmonic content, distortion, frequency deviations, unbalance voltage and current. Continuous monitor the power supply gives the quality of supply, identify the problems and provide the information of the system by using VI.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of decentralized IMC-PI controllers for real time coupled tank process
abstract: Decentralized Internal Model Control based Proportional-Integral controllers (IMC-PI) are designed and their performances are evaluated on a real time laboratory scale coupled tank process. It is a well known multi input multi output (MIMO) process with nonlinear behaviour. The experimental quad-coupled tank process is consisting of two upper and two lower tanks. The upper two tanks are connected with two pumps having varying speed drive for supplying water and they have an interacting behaviour with a connection in between them. In this work, our objective is to design and implement two IMC-PI controllers so that the water level can be maintained at the desired positions in the upper two tanks regardless of interaction among them. It is found that merely IMC-PI controllers fail to provide the satisfactory performance due to interaction among the tanks. To reduce interacting behaviour of the coupled tanks, a decoupler is incorporated during closed loop control. Performance of the proposed IMC-PI controllers are tested and compared in presence and absence of the designed decoupler. From the experimental results it is found that in presence of decoupler, IMC-PI controllers are found to provide an overall enhanced performance in maintaining the desired individual tank levels.

articleTitle: Sliding mode control algorithm with adaptive gain and implementation on inverted pendulum system
abstract: Sliding mode control algorithm is an efficient control strategy to control systems with bounded nonlinearities and parameter uncertainties. However, if the knowledge about the bounds is unknown, sliding mode control fails to guarantee its claimed robustness. The effects of external disturbances, with large magnitudes, can be tackled by using a high value for the controller gain, but with a consequence of increased level of chattering, an unwanted high frequency switching phenomenon occurring in the neighborhood of the sliding surface. In order to mitigate the above mentioned problems, an adaptive law is used to update the controller gain so that the sliding mode controller can track the desired output successfully. This paper demonstrates the design principles of a sliding mode controller with an adaptive law for updating the gain. The gain is so updated that the sliding mode algorithm successfully tracks the desired reference within finite time and does not overestimate the magnitude of external disturbances, thus preventing high level of chattering. The designed controller can track the desired reference value even if the bounds of the external disturbances are unknown. The controller is implemented on a mathematically modeled real time inverted pendulum system and the output responses are obtained. It is concluded that the sliding mode controller with adaptive gain can tackle systems with unknown bounds and also it takes care of the unwanted chattering effect.

articleTitle: Economic load dispatch using PSO and TLBO
abstract: This paper presents the application of Bio-inspired algorithms like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Teaching-learning Based Optimization (TLBO) for solution of economic load dispatch (ELD) problem. The algorithms are used to find the optimum solution with lowest fuel cost for four different network consisting of three, six, fifteen, and twenty generating units respectively for different load demand. Results obtained using PSO and TLBO are compared with the results obtained using lambda iteration method. The study has been done neglecting line losses as well as considering the line losses for different load demand. Both the algorithms are presented and described in this paper. The optimization has been done considering total fuel cost as the fitness function. The simulation results for all the cases are analyzed and presented in this paper.

articleTitle: An improved hybridization of Tournament and Genetic Algorithm for solving various Engineering design optimization problems
abstract: An improved hybrid algorithm of Tournament and Genetic Algorithm are presented for solving engineering design optimization problems. In our work, we have proposed an efficient hybrid algorithm based on tournament game concept and Genetic Algorithm, called the Tournament Genetic Algorithm (TGA), has been introduced for solving the classical optimization and Engineering design optimization problems. Five classical constrained optimization problems and two well known construction optimization problems have been solved and the corresponding outcomes were verified with other known optimization methods. Finally, to study the performance of our proposed technique with other well known optimization techniques, a comparative analysis has been made which are previously reported in the existing literature.

articleTitle: Modeling and testing of frequency adaptive phasor measurement unit
abstract: PMUs are the edifice of wide area monitoring and measurement system. The operation of PMU is essential to monitor and control the dynamic nature of the grid where voltage and current have constantly changing fundamental frequency due to change in load, generation imbalance, transients due to faults etc. Hence grid frequency is continuously varying about its nominal frequency therefore modeling of frequency adaptive PMU is significant. This paper aims to simulate a model of phasor measurement unit which helps to calculate phasors at off-nominal condition by adjusting sample values automatically using re-sampling filter, which is a more elegant than conventional anti-aliasing filter. The algorithm behind phasor estimation is DFT based and it is snuffed out in off-nominal condition, thus requiring the resampler. The performance of PMU is tested underwide variation of frequency to officiate the result.

articleTitle: A proposed method of load scheduling and generation control using GSM and PLCC technology
abstract: With the various advances in load forecasting techniques, now a day it is possible to perform load scheduling effectively. Modern day wireless communication techniques are replacing the older wire based systems. In this paper it is proposed to implement an automated system employing GSM & PLCC for the smooth operation of power generation & control. Load dispatch centre (LDC) will communicate with the individual power generation units & send scheduling based information through GSM techniques. The generation plants, in turn will actuate the scheduled data for their generation control using power line communication based SCADA system.

articleTitle: Electric field enhancement in an XLPE insulated power cable containing different voids and portrusions
abstract: This paper investigates the electric field enhancement created due to the presence of different types of voids and protrusions separately as well as simultaneously inside a polymeric insulated power cable. XLPE insulated power cables are used extensively in power systems as a preferred choice over traditional gas filled and impregnated paper insulated power cables. However, the presence of voids and cavities inside an insulation or on the semiconducting layer is unavoidable leading to an excessive field enhancement inside an insulation. This inevitably results in internal partial discharge and in a long run the failure of the entire cable insulation. For this contribution, the simulation of electric field is done on a two dimensional (2-D) model of a standard 22 kV XLPE insulation using Finite element analysis considering the effect of different voids and protrusions that may be present inside an insulation. Investigations reveal that the cable containing ellipsoidal protrusion with a cylindrical and elliptical void leads to a maximum field enhancement at the position of the void and at the surface respectively which is vulnerable for cable insulation.

articleTitle: Blended biogeography based optimization based LFC controller applied to multi-unit
abstract: This article proposes design and implementation of an evolutionary algorithm, named blended biogeography based optimization (BBBO), to solve load frequency control problem (LFC) in an interconnected power system network. Two area multi-unit multi-source power system network equipped with classical PI/PID controller is considered for the present study and dynamic responses of the same is investigated. The superiority and effectiveness of BBBO tuned PI/PID controller is examined by an extensive comparative analysis with the performance obtained by Zeigler Nichols (ZN) and genetic algorithm (GA) based classical controller, fuzzy gain scheduling (FGS), variable structure based FGS controller. The robustness of proposed controller is examined with different loading conditions and different performance indices. Furthermore, the study is extended to a nonlinear power system network considering governor dead band (GDB) and boiler dynamic nonlinearities.

articleTitle: Survey on major blackouts analysis and prevention methodologies
abstract: Power blackouts are major catastrophic failures in large inter connected power systems. Risk of blackouts is more than expected and must be considered in the power system studies. In past, many power blackouts occurredworldwide. An attempt has been made to summarize those major blackouts with their effects. To resolve the risk factors identified by the researchers various methodologies were proposed. This paper surveys major blackouts, analyze the reasons behind them and report major prevention methodologies proposed by various authors and aim at providing a broad perspective on blackouts in power system to researchers and application engineers. Classified manner in which the references are presented will serve them as quick and useful reference.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-PI control of motion tracking by an electrohydraulic system with multiple nonlinearities
abstract: The presence of uncertainties and nonlinearities in electrohydraulic actuation systems demand the use of astute controllers to achieve definitive motion tracking performance. Control methodologies based on mathematical models of such systems have been widely used to address these issues. However, such an approach necessitates an exquisite knowledge of the system parameters which is not always available, especially in harsh industrial environments. In this paper, a model free fuzzy approach has been introduced for tuning the gain parameters of a Proportional-Integral controller widely used in industries. Real-time experiments performed on a laboratory scale electrohydraulic actuation system reveals the robustness of the approach for conventional tracking demands up to high frequencies, even with the use of low cost industry grade proportional valve.

articleTitle: Combined speed and rotor resistance estimation for speed sensorless induction motor drive using reactive power based MRAS
abstract: The present work presents a combined estimation of speed and rotor resistance of an induction motor (IM) drive using model reference adaptive system (MRAS). The reactive power is used to generate the error signal for the adaptation mechanism in this MRAS. The reference model consists of the instantaneous reactive power computed by machine reference line current and voltages. Hence, the reference model is completely free from machine parameter variations. However, the steady state reactive power is used in the adaptive model which is free from flux and stator resistance terms. Thus, there is no requirement of estimation of flux making the system independent from integrator related problems like drift, saturation. Moreover, the absence of any derivative terms in the expression of steady state reactive power makes the system immune to noise. Hence, a stable operation at or near zero speed can be easily achieved. The uniqueness of this scheme is that in addition to speed estimation by the MRAS, another MRAS model is used for the on-line estimation of rotor resistance. This results in the accurate estimation of both the speed and rotor resistance simultaneously. The proposed scheme is developed in Matlab/Simulink. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Steady state modelling and ANFIS based analysis of doubly-fed induction generator
abstract: The paper presents a new technique for the steady state performance analysis of the DFIG using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). First, a mathematical model of DFIG in an appropriate d-q reference frame is established. The effect of the excitation voltage vector on the performance characteristics is illustrated to investigate simulations. A novel approach for the performance analysis of DFIG using ANFIS is employed for fast, accurate, and efficient methodology. The proposed ANFIS model has been trained off-line to predict the effect of excitation voltage magnitude, excitation voltage angle and speed on total output power of DFIG without overheating. The performance of the proposed scheme is investigated at different operating conditions. The simulation study indicates accuracy and effectiveness of the ANFIS based modelling of DFIG.

articleTitle: Adaptive Unscented Information filter for multiple sensor fusion
abstract: An adaptive nonlinear information filter for multiple sensor fusion is proposed in situations with nonlinear signal models and unknown process noise covariance. The proposed derivative free information filter, based on Unscented Transformation, ensures satisfactory estimation performance by online adaptation of the unknown process noise covariance. Efficacy of the proposed estimator is demonstrated with a well known object tracking problem in a sensor fusion configuration. From the results of Monte Carlo simulation it has been revealed that in the situation when the prior knowledge of the process noise covariance is lacking the performance of the proposed filter is demonstrably superior to its non adaptive version in the context of joint estimation of parameters and states.

articleTitle: A new Multi-Device Boost Converter topology with reduced switching stress and high voltage gain
abstract: This paper presents a novel Multi-Device Boost Converter (MDBC) topology having reduced switching stress and high voltage gain as compared to existing DC-DC boost converter topologies. The proposed topology is based on Capacitor-Inductor-Diode (CLD) cell configuration. Further, the proposed topology reduces the input current and output voltage ripples. A detailed simulation study in MATLAB/Simulink for the proposed converter has been done and compared with the existing topologies. This paper also presents a new topology based on interleaved converter with CLD cell.

articleTitle: Optimal location of TCSC and TCPS using hybrid DE/CRO algorithm
abstract: The optimal power flow (OPF) is an important area of power systems in which certain control variables are adjusted to minimize an objective function such as the cost of active power generation or the losses, while satisfying physical and operating constraints. The inclusion of FACTS devices in the power system network adds to its complexity. This paper presents a novel algorithm named hybridization of DE with CRO (DE/CRO) for solving the optimal placement and parameter setting of thyristor controlled series compensator (TCSC) and thyristor controlled phase shifter (TCPS) to achieve optimal performance of power system network. The proposed method is tested and validated for locating TCSC and TCPS in IEEE 30-bus test system. Results show that the proposed method is good to select proper location of TCSC and TCPS for secured OPF.

articleTitle: An analysis of economic load dispatch with prohibited zone constraint using different algorithms
abstract: Economic load dispatch (ELD) problem plays an important role in power system operation and control today. It is very popular optimization problem in advanced power system. Recently different soft computing techniques are being widely used in many practical applications. Here, fifteen thermal unit system has been considered. This problem has been solved by four types of PSO based optimization problem like particle swarm optimization technique(PSO), particle swarm optimization with constriction factor approach(PSOCFA), particle swarm optimization technique with inertia weight factor approach(PSOIWA) and particle swarm optimization technique with constriction factor and inertia weight factor approach(PSOCFIWA). In this problem, prohibited zone constraint has been considered. In this paper, successful implementation and effectiveness of four types of optimization technique has been shown to solve this problem. The comparative analysis of fuel cost through four optimization techniques has been discussed.

articleTitle: A comparison study between stereotypical Multilevel-inverters with Multistring inverter in three-phase loaded condition
abstract: This paper presents a recently developed, popular and efficient Multi-level Inverter (MLI) known as MultistringMLI (MMLI). This topology not only demands lesser switches but also provide superior quality of output waveform with lesser THD and good fundamental RMS value than that of conventional converters. So for the very first time it has been compared with all stereotypical MLIs in three-phase loaded condition. For five level output, MMLI needs two numbers of lesser switches in each phase than conventional MLIs. Although with increase with levels no of switches increases, but at the same time the difference of no of required switches among the conventional converters and MMLI also increases. This is the best advantage of MMLI. In the study all the simulation has been carried out for fivelevels only in three phase loaded condition. From the study it has been demonstrated that how it maintains more and equal quality of output waveform irrespective of switching frequencies. All the output voltage levels also have been mathematically derived.

articleTitle: Network contingency ranking using analytic hierarchy process to calculate unequal importance factors for static severity indices
abstract: Network contingency analysis for power system operation, is considered as the most vital concern of its security appraisal. Present days, on-line security assessment is carried out by contingency ranking, with the help of various computing techniques. One of the iterative methods is Newton Raphson power flow method for obtaining the magnitudes of different parameters. The aim of contingency ranking is to create a short list of possible potential threats quickly and rank them according to their severity in an accurate manner. A static security assessment dependent approach is presented in this paper for contingency ranking, incorporating analytic hierarchy process as an improvement to the conventional power flow based ranking techniques. The proposed method is employed to choose proper unequal importance factors for the weighted severity index. The usefulness of the technique has been verified on IEEE 14 bus system and the results are presented with a detailed comparison, with the help of Network Graphical Overlays for pre and post-contingent states of power system.

articleTitle: Design of adaptive two-degree-of-freedom controller for inversion based reference input tracking of non-minimum phase system
abstract: This paper presents a novel technique towards inversion based reference input tracking control problem of non-minimum phase system which has unstable dynamics. Exact set point tracking can be possible by using inversion based system, but it is restricted to minimum phase systems only; whereas in case of non-minimum phase (NMP) system the concept of inversion technique gives unstable output response. To overcome this problem, a two-degrees-of-freedom (2DOF) control technique has been applied here for inversion based reference input tracking control problem of NMP system. It is shown that the combination of Model Reference Adaptive Control structure (MRAC) using MIT rule and state feedback control methodology in 2DOF framework can track the reference input trajectory of NMP system employing the inversion based technique with a small steady state error. Initial undershoot is an undesirable characteristic of NMP system which has also been minimized. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been established in simulation studies.

articleTitle: Statistical feature based child emotion analysis
abstract: Children are vulnerable and express emotions very often. Their emotional contents in speech can resemble more closely to natural emotions. On the other hand, emotions of elderly people are highly biased and stimulated. In order to capture emotions more closely by an efficient recognition system real emotions can play a vital role. Motivated by this the authors have attempted with child speech emotion for this task. Mostly used prosodic and spectral features have been extracted at first. Statistical analysis was carried out to increase the robustness of the feature sets. An Indigenous children database to categorize four emotional states as angry, happy, sad, and surprise was developed. Radial basis function network has been used for training purpose and the results were compared with different combination of emotions. Results show a decrease in recognition accuracy with increase in number of emotions used for classification.

articleTitle: Grey wolf optimizer for Short term Hydrothermal Scheduling problems
abstract: This paper presents Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) Algorithm in order to solve Short-term Hydro-Thermal Scheduling (SHTS) problems. With large number of variables the non-linearity of the search space of SHTS problem increases and most algorithms are not capable to give enough diversity in the crowds of swarms for finding better solutions. However, the unique characteristic of GWO algorithm increases the diversity in solutions and the search capability. The performance of the proposed algorithm is experimented on two short term multi reservoir cascaded hydrothermal systems. First test case is moderately large while the second test case is a considerably large one. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed algorithm as compared to other recently reported ones in terms of convergence and better quality of solutions.

articleTitle: Design and modeling of a novel two - stage cascaded Interleaved Boost Converter for high voltage applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel two - stage cascaded Interleaved Boost Converter is proposed. A steady state mathematical model for the same has been developed on MATLAB / SIMULINK. This converter provides a high voltage output which is intended to power a three - phase inverter which subsequently drives a three - phase AC load. The input considered is from a 48V battery or solar panel. The output DC link voltage is about 532V. Conventional Interleaved Boost Converter becomes uncontrollable due to very high duty ratio for switching these voltage levels. Hence, a novel two - stage cascaded Interleaved Boost Converter has been proposed. It has been designed for a power output of 1kW. The authors have made an effort to justify the choice of two - stage cascaded Interleaved Boost Converter by simulating and comparing various boost converter topology combinations and it is shown that the chosen topology is the best option from the view of reduced output voltage ripple (0.05V), current ripple (<;0.2A), simplicity of design and improved conversion efficiency. The simulated output values of the steady state mathematical model are verified with the designed values.

articleTitle: Simulation of Vector Controlled Induction Motor Drive in MATLAB for various applications: A comparative study
abstract: This paper presents a detailed performance analysis and comparative study of Vector Controlled Induction Motor Drive (VCIMD) for different industrial applications in MATLAB environment using Simulink and Sim Power System (SPS) toolboxes in Discrete Time Frame. Various operating conditions such as start mode, brake mode, reversal of speed, step change in speed command, etc., have been considered from the application viewpoint. Analysis of such operating conditions lead towards a check for sustainability for various industrial applications such as conveyors, feeders, fan load, pump load, etc., wherein the choice of a three-phase squirrel cage induction motor introduces simplicity, robustness and a maintenance free environment leading to an economic solution with increase of efficiency. In realizing such an analysis, the paper also processes a comparison between the various control strategies used for converting the feedback signal to a reference command for torque and flux which are electrically de-coupled to operate the current controlled (CC) voltage source inverter (VSI) fed induction motor like a separately excited, compensated, DC motor.

articleTitle: Real time Prony Analysis for fast detection of harmonics and interharmonics in a power electronic converter
abstract: Power electronic converters, used for improving efficiency, distort the line voltage and current waveforms leading to power quality issues. An effective and fast estimation of harmonics and interharmonics, is thus needed. This paper highlights the use of Prony Analysis in real time for determination of frequency components. A comparison with FFT shows that this method is successful in detecting all such harmonics and interharmonics within a much smaller window thus making this a faster alternative.

articleTitle: Design and modeling of Z Source Inverter with the novel implementation of modified modulating signal and shoot through control strategies
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Z Source Inverter (ZSI) and a novel switching pulse implementation is adapted for the same. A steady state mathematical model for the ZSI has been developed on MATLAB/SIMULINK. The Conventional Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (CSVPWM) can be viewed as a modified form of Sine triangle PWM (SPWM). The present work utilizes the modified modulating signal generated using a simple algorithm. The switching pulses for the three phases of ZSI are obtained by the inclusion of the shoot through state using two control strategies - Simple Boost Control (SBC) and Maximum Boost Control (MBC). The boosted DC link voltage obtained from the impedance source network is intended to power a three phase inverter which can in turn drive a three phase AC load. The dc input voltage to the Z source network is 210V. An attempt has been made by the authors to simulate the ZSI with modified modulating signal and a mathematical model has been developed to verify the boost functionality with the two control strategies. Three phase 50Hz ac output voltage obtained from the ZSI schematic circuit has an rms value of 410.12V (with SBC) and 413.65V (with MBC).

articleTitle: Improved tuning of cascade controllers for stable and integrating processes with time delay
abstract: In process industries, cascade control is one of the commonly used techniques to improve the performance of a single loop control structure when there are disturbances associated with the manipulated variable. In the present work, tuning rules have been proposed for series cascade control structure considering stable and integrating process models with time delay. The primary controller is a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller in series with a lead/lag filter whereas the secondary controller is a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller. The direct synthesis approach is used to design both the controllers. The main advantage of the proposed tuning strategy is that it yields improved regulatory performance than some recently reported tuning strategies. Simulation examples are given to illustrate the superiority of the proposed scheme as compared to the recently reported tuning strategies.

articleTitle: Radar assessment of wavelet decomposition based Skewness of ECG signals
abstract: This paper deals with the Skewness based assessment of ECG signals. Electrocardiogram signals of a normal healthy person and a patient suffering from Myocardial Ischemia are collected for assessment. This has been done by first, collecting normal ECG signal collected then de-noising by passing it through well-known Savitzky-Golay FIR filter. Then Skewness values of detail coefficients of the normal ECG signal at different DWT decomposition level is measured. Then, real ECG signal collected from a heart patient and is then de-noised by passing it through wellknown Savitzky-Golay FIR filter. Then Skewness values of detail coefficients of this real ECG signal at different DWT decomposition level is determined. Radars of Skewness values of detail coefficients of the de-noised normal and real ECG signal at different DWT decomposition level are formed. It shows clear and distinct difference of radars of skewness of detail coefficients of the de-noised normal and real ECG signal with different DWT decomposition level.

articleTitle: Estimation of vehicle yaw rate and lateral motion for dynamic stability control using unscented Kalman filtering (UKF) approach
abstract: The increasing demand for passenger safety and comfort has inspired to develop technologically sophisticated automobiles that provide improved vehicle handling. In automotive industry, current focus is on the development of active safety systems, which assist the driver in order to avoid critical situations. Unfortunately, some fundamental states which are valuable for the vehicle dynamics control systems are not measurable or uneconomical. Hence, the states are to be estimated. This paper presents the estimation of yaw rate and lateral motion/velocity, which are among the essential states. A simplified model of the vehicle during a DLC turning maneuver is been considered and the dynamic equations of the states were summed up. Thereafter, they were estimated using non-linear UKF approach. Computer simulation have been conducted to verify the proposed approach, with results indicating that the proposed approach is very effective and robust in estimating yaw rate and lateral dynamics.

articleTitle: Inter turn fault diagnosis of three phase induction motor using SST and KNN
abstract: In this paper, an on line fault diagnosis of stator inter turn fault of 3-Φ induction motor is presented. The fault diagnosis technique uses only time synchronized samples of three phase stator current signals, from which the positive and negative sequence components are calculated by Sample Shifting technique (SST). A KNN based fault detection algorithm is made in MATLAB to diagnosis the inter turn fault and faulty phase. The main objective of this work is to establish a system capable of detecting the stator condition of Induction motor by continuous monitoring of stator current. The proposed work is simulated by modeling a three phase induction motor model with inter turn fault condition in MATLAB. To check the accuracy of algorithm, this method is verified experimentally on a 0.5 HP, 415 V, 3-Φ Induction motor.

articleTitle: A new wavelet and fuzzy based power quality index for distribution systems under stationary and nonstationary disturbances
abstract: The evaluation of power quality is needed due to the prolification of disturbing loads in the electric power systems. In the past few years there has been an increase of the distortion level in distribution systems due to the development of non linear loads. In this paper a novel power quality index has been introduced which can evaluate the power quality under stationary and nonstationary disturbances Three power system components has been considered, representative quality power factor, detail pollution factor and standard deviation of the signal for the development of the new power quality index. The proposed power quality index has been applied to different cases, sinusoidal, non sinusoidal, linear, non linear, stationary and non stationary waveforms. It has been found that new power quality index can completely characterize the power system disturbances both qualitatively and quantitatively.

articleTitle: Advantage of Unscented Kalman Filter over Extended Kalman Filter in dynamic state estimation of power system network
abstract: The Kalman filter is a set of mathematical equations which are used to estimate the state of a system by minimizes the mean of the squared error. In this paper Kalman filtering is used for the estimation of states of IEEE 14 bus power system network. Here we considered dynamic states i.e. rotor angle in radians and speed in rad/sec of all the generators present in the system. We mainly focus on the advantages of Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) over Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) by comparing both estimation methods. In EKF state distribution is approximated by a Gaussian Random Variable (GRV), which is then propagated analytically through a first order linearization of the non-linear system. This introduces errors in posteriori mean and covariance of the transformed GRV, which may lead to suboptimal performance of the filter. The UKF addresses this problem by using a deterministic sampling approach. In this paper these two algorithms are tested on an IEEE-14 bus,5-generator test system by applying test cases like sudden load change and configuration topology error to show how adaptive these filters during those conditions.

articleTitle: Performance assessment of different singlephase multi-level inverter
abstract: Use of multilevel inverter is becoming a trend in the recent years for high power applications. Various topologies and its assessment have been reported for recent literature. Power quality is an important phenomenon in the high power electric circuit and thus suitable topology must be selected for optimum result. Two multilevel inverter topology with the basic bridge configuration of single phase inverter have been analyzed on various parameters and the result are conclude based on the simulation model design from PSIM.

articleTitle: Fault detection in synchrophasor system by using Phasor Measuring Unit
abstract: In order to prevent large scale cascading failure, continuous measuring and monitoring of the system in real time is necessary for secure and reliable operation of the interconnected Power Grid system. The actual analog signal has to be sampled to establish the fundamental frequency within a specific frequency zone. With the help of that frequency, the signal is reconstructed at time domain of fundamental frequency tone and dynamic phasors of the system are estimated by using Phasor Measuring Unit. The objective of this paper is to determine proper algorithm of the Phasor Measuring Unit and detection of fault within a specified time when disturbance occurs in the system.

articleTitle: Analytical modeling and simulation of Work Function Engineered gate junctionless high-k dielectric Double Gate MOSFET: A comparative study
abstract: Over the years, the approach of cylindrical gate MOSFETs has attracted several research initiatives due to the very inherent benefit of the cylindrical geometry over other conventional planar structures. Nowadays, the present boon in the research field of nanoscale device physics in attributed to a large extent by the development of novel devices without junctions. This work presents a two dimensional analytical modeling of a novel junctionless Work Function Engineered high-k dielectric Double Gate MOSFET structure to formulate a simplified expression for short channel threshold voltage. Based on the analytical calculations, an overall performance analysis of our proposed device having high-k (HfO2) gate oxide has been investigated to establish the superiority of our proposed structure in terms of superior Short Channel Effect (SCE) mitigation and a significant reduction in threshold voltage. The results obtained from our analytical analysis are found to be in good agreement with the simulation results, which validates the accuracy of our model.

articleTitle: Zero dynamics design of excitation controller with comparison to H∞ design in power system stability improvement
abstract: This paper proposes a nonlinear control strategy for enhancement of dynamic stability of a power system. The zero dynamic design theory of feedback linearization is employed to design the Nonlinear Excitation Controller (NEC). The performance of this nonlinear controller has been compared with the performance of robust excitation controller for different operating scenarios of a Single Machine Infinite Bus (SMIB) power system. The mixed-sensitivity based Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) approach with pole placement constraint has been adopted to design the H∞ controller. Simulation studies interpret that the proposed nonlinear controller and the H∞ controller are both effective in power system stability improvements, regardless of the operating points. It has been further observed that the performance of the nonlinear excitation controller is significantly better than the robust H∞ controller.

articleTitle: Analysis of electro-cardiogram by radar and DWT based Kurtosis comparison
abstract: This paper deals with the electro-cardiogram analysis by radar and discrete wavelet transformation based Kurtosis assessment of electrocardiogram signals. Electrocardiogram signals of a normal healthy person and a patient suffering from Myocardial Ischemia are collected for assessment. First, normal ECG signal collected and is then de-noised by passing it through well-known Savitzky-Golay FIR filter. Then the signal is decomposed at different discrete wavelt transform (DWT) levels Kurtosis of approximate coefficients of the normal ECG signal at different DWT decomposition level is measured. Then, real ECG signal collected from patient suffering from heart disease and is de-noised Savitzky-Golay FIR filter. Then Kurtosis of approximate coefficients of this signal at different DWT decomposition level is measured. Radars of Variation of Kurtosis of approximate coefficients of the de-noised normal and real signals and radars are compared. It shows clear and distinct difference of radars of Kurtosis of detail coefficients of the de-noised normal and real ECG signal with different DWT decomposition level.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of cascaded MLI based PV system using Sub-multilevel cells
abstract: The conversion process in non-conventional energy system play a vital role looking to the utilization factors at the consumer site. Hence in this paper the entire focus has been diverted to the conversion process of PV system. The conversion process includes here a multi-level inverter which is modeled through MATLAB/SIMULINK. The MLI is using reduced number of switches which helps to reduce harmonic content and in return quality of power improves. In this paper comparative analysis on THD has been made between 25 level and 49 level inverter and it is found that using 16 number of switches on 49 level MLI instead of 12 switches on 25 level MLI the THD content reduced to nearly 1% from 3.2% in 25 level MLI.

articleTitle: An accurate electrical parameters optimization of three phase induction machine considering core loss resistance
abstract: An appropriate methodology of parameters calculation of induction motor is very important for high performance speed control drive. Several paper were produced earlier neglecting the core loss resistance while calculating the parameter of Induction motor. In this study, a novel implementation technique is proposed to considering the core loss resistance non linearity. This paper proposes a general idea of finding the parameters of induction motor through no load and block rotor test giving due consideration to core loss resistance Rc . The paper also describes the problem of considering the assumptions made in earlier literature and attempt to propose a generalize view of three phase induction motor. For three phase induction motor, value of core loss resistance Rc is found iteratively to find out its actual operating point. Simulation results followed by experimental result confirm the validity of our proposed expressions.

articleTitle: Application of PSO for optimizing gain parameters of a controller in real system
abstract: In this paper, a method for designingthe optimal proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller parameters of a permanent magnet DC Motor using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is presented. The proposed approach has advantages like easy implementation, fast convergence and good computational efficiency. If compared to the conventional Ziegler-Nichols Tuning approach, the proposed PSO-PID parameter design approach was having good time response, much robust in use and numerically efficient.

articleTitle: A wind based micro-generation and storage scheme at low wind speeds using single-phase induction machine
abstract: In this paper, a wind power based low voltage generation and storage scheme has been established for low wind speeds. A single-phase induction machine is run as standalone induction generator for single-phase generation. The generated energy is stored in Lead-acid storage batteries via a single-phase bridge rectifier which can later be retrieved for feeding loads. A suitable algorithm for the storage battery is also developed following the State-of-Charge (SOC) of the battery. The proposed scheme can be suitable for micro-wind applications in remote and grid inaccessible areas. An energy management scheme for the proposed system is also developed in the paper. The reliability for such a generation and storage scheme is tested using suitable simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Skewness based voltage sag assessment in power systems
abstract: This paper deals with the assessment of voltage sag for power quality analysis. For this purpose different voltage signals having different percentages of sag have been simulated and then by Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) based Skewness analysis is done to detect the voltage sag condition. After that interpolation or extrapolation have been done for unknown Skewness values for assessment of voltage sag. Using this unique technique very optimistic result has come out for assessment of voltage sag in power quality disturbance analysis and which can be applied in real time systems.

articleTitle: Stabilization of time-delay systems with Lipschitz nonlinearities using LSVF control
abstract: This paper investigates the stabilization problem for a class of Lipschitz nonlinear time-delay systems. With the useful information extracted from the Lipschitz nonlinearity of the system and employing a Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional, Linear State Feedback Controller design conditions have been derived and expressed in terms of linear matrix inequalities. The designed state feedback controller ensures closed loop stability of the nonlinear time-delay system. To test the effectiveness of the proposed control methodology, control law is employed for a liquid monopropellant rocket motor with a pressure feeding system.

articleTitle: Detection and characterisation of QRS complex in VMD domain
abstract: Automatic localisation of ECG signal features for detection of abnormalities is recently flashed a remarkable research work. However with the promising result of the analysis there is much space of improvements in terms of accuracy. In this work a part of ventricular activity in cardiac cycle is addressed to establish the morphological characteristics of the segmental ECG signal. Here ventricular QRS complex of the ECG signal is analysed in frequency domain by Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) technique. The purpose of this work is to extract the QRS complex from raw ECG data without pre-processing. This method is tested on MIT-BIH arrhythmia data base and a comprehensive result is established with an accuracy of more than 99%.

articleTitle: Synthesis of parameter dependency performance of saturated iron-core superconducting fault current limiter
abstract: In modern power systems, fault current limiters (FCL) are used to provide protection against high fault currents during electrical faults and thereby, help serve an uninterrupted supply of electricity to the consumers. Among the various technologies available for FCLs, the saturated iron-core superconducting fault current limiter (SISFCL) has gained a lot of attention on account of its ability to provide very low impedance during normal operation and a high impedance during fault condition. This is achieved by utilizing the change in magnetic state of the ferromagnetic cores between saturation and unsaturation. In this paper, the responses of an SISFCL is analyzed for variations of different parameters, namely, the fault resistance, DC bias current, number of turns of the AC coil and number of turns of the DC coil. Further analysis is also done to study the SISFCL's responses for different B-H characteristics of core materials. The analyses are performed using a mathematical model in MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of Fuzzy tuned Proportional Resonant controller for Shunt Active Power filter using Neutral Point Clamped Multi-level Inverter
abstract: Recent trend in the power distribution system is showing that the use of non-linear loads and devices will take a rising profile in days to come. This introduces harmonics in source side currents which degrades the power quality. Power utilities are very much concerned with this situation. The use of Shunt Active Power filters (SAPF) is one of the wellknown solutions. In this paper the reference compensating currents are generated using P-Q theory. The DC link capacitor voltage control is done using Fuzzy tuned Proportional Resonant (PR) controller. The capacitor plays the role of energy source element so its voltage control is a vital part in this scheme. The inverter used for SAPF is of Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) Multilevel Inverter which in turn reduces the dv/dt stress on the devices and they can be operated with lower switching frequency resulting in lower switching losses. The Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) obtained in this scheme is smaller than those obtained with other different controlling techniques available. The simulation results are analysed and justified which shows the usefulness of this strategy.

articleTitle: A novel method based on Complex Network theory approach for location of Distributed Generators in radial distribution systems
abstract: With the advancement of Smart Grid and Distributed Generation, the complications of power transfer over long distances have been reduced as the need and independent energy production is met. Here a technique of analysing the location of a distributed generation in a distribution system of a grid is applied based on Complex Network theory. The metric of Electrical Centrality is the approach used in differentiating the physical and electrical topological structure. Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bus</sub> represents the electrical strength of connection of every node to every other node in the network and hence this Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bus</sub> matrix represents the more electrically central nodes which signify for best location for distributed generation in a distribution system by an exhaustive search. We obtain results for an 85 node radial distribution systems. The location of Distributed Generators also makes overall system losses very small and successfully corrects voltage profile.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation of three phase induction motor using gravitational search algorithm for IFOC
abstract: This Paper presents dynamic parameter estimation of a three phase induction motor based on gravitational search algorithm (GSA) and Indirect Field Oriented Control (IFOC) methodology. The IFOC and Induction motor are modelled in MATLAB (Simulink) environment and the GSA algorithm has adopted for this parameter estimation purposes. The parameters like rotor resistance, time varying inductances etc. are estimated to have a better control over the running of the induction motor. It has been seen that the proposed method is efficient enough with enhanced accuracy in the estimation of parameters.

articleTitle: Tuning rules for fractional order controllers for integrating and unstable process models
abstract: A set of new tuning rules for fractional-order controllers for integrating and unstable processes are proposed in this study. The tuning rules are proposed in order to minimize the IST2E performance criterion. Furthermore, analytical expressions are devised for the optimal values of the performance indexes. The performance indexes may be used to assess the controller performance for a given process model. The controller in its series form has been considered while proposing the set of tuning rules.Simulation results show that improved servo and regulatory performance is achieved by the proposed tuning rules as compared to the recently reported approaches.

articleTitle: Assessment of harmonic voltage angles in a multi-bus power system during symmetrical fault at certain bus
abstract: The basic function of electrical power system is to convert electrical energy from some universal form to electrical form, which may be consumed locally, or can be transmitted from one location to other. During power delivery and transmission, ideally frequency should be constant, but in real time applications, it is a variable notation. This variance sometimes makes the angular bus voltage differences erratic, rendering into irregular behaviour of a network. This paper deals with the estimation of change of harmonic voltage angles in a multi-bus network for fundamental, harmonic and symmetrical short circuit fault conditions of the network. The changes found have been analyzed and feature extraction has been done to identify the fault bus in the network.

articleTitle: Automatic generation control of an interconnected hydro-thermal system using chemical reaction optimization
abstract: In this article, a maiden effective approach named, chemical reaction optimization (CRO) in tuning the proportional-plus-integral (PI) controller is suggested for automatic generation control (AGC) of a two-area hydro thermal power system. The comparison of the optimum values obtained for the PI parameters by the proposed method is compared with that obtained by other population based optimization techniques lke biogeography based optimization (BBO), differential evolution (DE) and genetic algorithm (GA) to show the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the system performance. The simulation results show that the objective function value keeps on decreasing much faster and gives a better value compared to that obtained by other reported algorithms. This implies that CRO improves the dynamic performance of the system and has better convergence characteristics as compared to the BBO, DE and GA techniques, proving the superiority of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of a SSSC-based damping controller
abstract: This paper deals with the performance analysis of a damping controller for a Static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) for enhancing the power system dynamic stability of a single machine power system connecting to an infinite bus. Following a disturbance in the power system, there will be a miss-match between the input mechanical and output electrical power of the machine which leads to the deviation in the rotor angle as well as the rotor speed. The controller takes any one of this deviation and processed it in to a compensating voltage injected in series by the SSSC. The tuning of the controller is done by a nature inspired optimizing technique called as firefly algorithm. Further, the controller performance is analyzed and is verified for different disturbance conditions.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of CdS/CdTe heterojunction thin film solar cell
abstract: In this paper, we are reporting the fabrication andthe characterization of a CdS/CdTe based hetero-junction thin film solar cell. Indium tin oxide (ITO) and aluminum (Al) were used as front and back contacts respectively. CdS, CdTe and Al were coated on ITO coated glass substrate by using thermal coating unit. Here in CdS/CdTe based hetero-junction solar cell, CdS acts as window layer and CdTe acts as absorbing layer. Optical characterization such as transmission, reflection, absorption were carried out to determine the band gap of CdTe and CdS which observed to be 1.32 eV and 2.38eV respectively. SEM and I-V characterization were performed to investigate the structural and electrical properties of the heterojunction solar cell.

articleTitle: A proposed DC line current measurement technique based on current induced magnetic field sensing using n-channel enhancement-type MOSFET
abstract: In this paper, a DC line current measurement technique by sensing the magnetic field due to the steady current flowing through the line has been proposed. A circuit in which the n-channel enhancement-type MOSFET is used as magnetic field sensor is designed and tested for a wide range of DC line currents. The circuit is capable of measuring both the magnitude and direction of the DC current flowing through a line without any direct electrical contact. BS170 n-channel enhancement type MOSFET is used as magnetic field sensor. Experimental results are very encouraging to use this technique for measuring wide range of DC line currents without making any electrical contact.

articleTitle: Control of chaos in BLDC motor using modified feedback method
abstract: This paper is concerned with the chaotic behavior of brushless dc(BLDC) motor and its control. The chaotic behavior of BLDC motor plays a vital role on the controllability of the system with BLDC motor. The proposed controller is to suppress the chaotic behavior of BLDC motor and to terminate the motor in the desired state. The controller is designed with modified care to obtain the guaranteed global stability. The simulation results of the controlled system show that the system can be escaped from the chaotic states and stay in the desired state. Due to its inherent simplicity and straight forwardness the controller can be implemented in a simple hardware.

articleTitle: Investigation of thermo-physical properties of 1-hexyl-3-mythyl imidazolium bromide using 2D triangular photonic crystal structure
abstract: In this paper, thermo-physical properties of 1-hexyl-3-methyl imidazolium bromide in their aqueous solution are thoroughly investigated using 2D triangular photonic crystal structure. The thermo-physical properties are realized by concentration, water activity and vapour pressure of 1-hexyl-3-methyl imidazolium bromide in their aqueous solution. The photonic bandgap of photonic crystal structure is a key parameter to accomplish such properties, which is simulated by employing plane wave expansion (PWE) method. Simulation result revealed that both photonic bandgap of triangular photonic crystal structure and transmitted energy emerging from such structure vary linearly with respect to different thermophysical parameters. This excellent linear variation leads to an accurate investigation of aforementioned thermo physical properties in their aqueous solution.

articleTitle: A novel gene expression programming based ECG biometric scheme
abstract: These are the days of cloud computing, bigdata analysis, smart phones all around and 24x7 internet connectivity. This has both pros and cons of so much of data all around. Therefore securities of these data are a major concern as well. Present day trend is to use our biological information as a key for biometrics, human computer interaction, biomimetics, etc. Of these biometrics are the most popularly used most of the time it is based on fingerprints or iris as they are the most commonly used types. With every new advanced technology comes up another new technology to counter it. The parallel research is going on to both enhance and breach securities or at least override them. Thus instead of one biometric a few more are clubbed together to form multimodal biometrics to enhance security. Electrocardiogram or ECG is one such biometric which has given great results when used as a multimodal biometric, along with its other popular counterparts. This is because it provides easy aliveness detection. Here it is used as a single biometric characteristic using a novel gene expression programming (GEP) based recognition scheme. That too has been done on a single ECG lead to make the process of implementation user friendly.

articleTitle: An extensive simulation study of Cylindrical Surrounding Gate MOSFET (DMCSG-MOSFET) with gate misalignment
abstract: In this paper, 2D Dual Material Cylindrical Surrounding Gate MOSFET (DMCSG-MOSFET) has been modelled using SENTAURUS TCAD device simulator. The effect of gate misalignment at the source and drain end of DMCSG-MOSFET has been investigated. The variation of electrical parameters such as drain current, leakage current, threshold voltage and sub-threshold slope due to the increase in misalignment length at both ends has been studied. However the above results are compared to the conventional cylindrical MOSFET.

articleTitle: CHPV control
abstract: Localised energy systems featuring distributed generation technologies such as combined heat and power and photovoltaics present a significant integration challenge due to simultaneous generation of both thermal and electrical energy. Control of energy storage provides a potential solution to this problem by absorbing surplus energy production and providing extra energy if the balance is in deficit. This paper presents a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) error actuated method of controlling distributed energy storage for localised energy systems featuring a combined heat and power engine plus building integrated solar PV array with twin objectives of maintaining a defined operative temperature while simultaneously maintaining a prescribed electrical profile. Impact of IT and emerging integrated DC systems in buildings, including ICT and LED lighting are considered. Performance of the control strategy is assessed using heat demands generated by calibrated commercial building models for a single zone developed in a Matlab/ Simulink environment. Results are presented and discussed in context of integrated CHPV systems design and operational performance against conventional heat and power systems.

articleTitle: Modelling of a directly coupled PV Water Pumping System using Soft Computing techniques
abstract: Photo-Voltaic Water Pumping System (PVWPS) is the most suitable system for low head irrigation in the remote areas. PVWPS may be characterized by its multivariable-nonlinear equations; however, efficient water demand management necessitates fast and accurate water flow rate estimation at actual operating states. This can hardly be achieved with conventional mathematical -based methodologies. In this paper two of the Soft Computing (SC) techniques are due selected; Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) for PVWPS novel modeling and performance pre-evaluation .The (ANN) model and (ANFIS) models are trained off-line to identify the water flow rate based on air temperature, solar irradiation, and static head as input parameters. An iteration technique which is mathematical-based is also presented for comparison and evaluation purposes. The paper indicates accuracy, robustness and effectiveness of the proposed models in water flow rate control, economic feasibility and fault detection.

articleTitle: Active power loss minimization by harmony search algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a recently developed optimization technique named as harmony search algorithm (HSA). Objective of the proposed work is to minimize the active power loss. This algorithm is tested on standard IEEE 14 and 30bus test system for the determination of optimal setting of control/design variables such as tap setting of transformer, reactive var generation of generator buses and reactive power generated by the shunt capacitor with different HS parameters. Addition of the shunt capacitors at weak buses are identified by the weak bus analysis.

articleTitle: Phase disposition PWM five-level inverter short switch diagnosis using DWT and ANN
abstract: The paper presents a short-switch fault diagnosis scheme for a cascaded five-level inverter with phase disposition PWM using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The Multi Resolution Analysis (MRA) property of DWT is used for the extraction of the detailed components form the inverter line-to-line voltage and subsequently, these are used for the computation of energy at each level. Additionally, various voltage ratios from the line-to-line voltage are computed. In fact, line-to-line voltage is independent of the nature of load and hence, it is considered as the analysing signal. The voltage ratios together with the calculated energies are considered as the important features for the ANN training for short-switch faults. The whole scheme is implemented by simulation in Matlab/ Simulink. The simulation results show that the scheme successfully identifies the short switch fault for any switch health conditions. Moreover, the scheme is simple and does not involve too many computations. This ensures the real time applicability of the proposed algorithm in any fast acting digital signal processor. The scheme is universal and can be applied to any other inverter topology as well.

articleTitle: Analysis and solution of nonlinear two-dimensional Volterra integro differential equation of second kind using block pulse function: A review
abstract: This paper deals with idea of solving nonlinear VolterraFredholm integral and integro differential equations of second kind using orthogonal block pulse function approach. The efficient way of solving higher order differential equations using block pulse function approach provides a strong foundation to apply this technique to solve nonlinear equations like Volterra and Fredholm integral equations, which appears most frequently in electromagnetic field theory, image processing, stereography, radiography and cosmic radiation. A comparative study is prepared between exact response obtained through either ADM, MADM, successive approximation, series solution, direct computation method and the repose obtained by PCOBPF. Verification of the procedure is carried out by few illustrative examples.

articleTitle: A comparative study between different multi level inverter topologies for different types of bus clamping PWM techniques using Six Region Selection Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a modified region selection algorithm called “Newly-Modified Six-Region (NMSR)” selection technique for implementing different types of Bus-Clamped PWM (BCPWM) techniques i.e. Type-1, Type-2, Type-3 and Type-4 BCPWM for three-level Voltage Source Inverter (VSI). The novelty of the proposed algorithm is that it can be applied to any level of inverters with much easier and lesser computations. An extensive comparison study between different topologies of Multilevel Inverters (MLI) has been done with different types of BCPWM techniques implemented by the proposed NMSR technique. It has been observed that the advantages of BCPWM compared to Conventional Space Vector PWM (CSVPWM) technique remain unaltered which signifies the effectiveness of the proposed technique. Further it also observed that the flying capacitor topology performs better compare to other conventional topologies and Type-4 BCPWM technique gives better quality of output waveforms with lesser Total Harmonic Distortion (THD).

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Type-I based person identification
abstract: Automatic person identification problem attracts significant popularity in the last decade in the field of human-robot interaction. This paper addresses a novel approach to recognize a person automatically whom the robot has already met, based on its walking pattern as gait is a unique characteristic for every individual.
