Here, we have used the Kinect sensor to record the gait pattern of a person by storing 20 3-D joint coordinates at each time stamps. A simple method to detect a complete gait cycle is proposed. The significant features like joint angle and joint length are obtained from each complete walk cycle. Later, these features are fuzzified constructing a Gaussian membership function with the mean and standard deviation of each feature at different trial for a single subject. 10 walking data set of ten subjects are processed here. Now, when any person out of these ten persons is walking in front of Kinect, features are calculated which are considered as measurement point. Defuzzification is done using t-norm operator. The person corresponding to highest defuzzified value is considered as the unknown person. Later, a novel adaption procedure of the membership functions is proposed to tune their width. The classification accuracy is 86.25%. The proposed method is also compared with few existing person identification techniques and the results obtained prove the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Phasor measurement unit allocation with different soft computing technique inconnected power network
abstract: PMUs are necessity tools for monitoring the system condition at specific measurement location of the connected power grid. The optimal PMU placement (OPP) problem refer to the perseverance of the minimum number of PMUs and their corresponding locations concerning to achieve full network observability. This paper introduces different soft computing technique to solve the OPP problem using Power System Analysis Toolbox (PSAT), a Matlab toolbox. The case study has been carried out on IEEE 6, 9, 14 and 30-bus test systems and obtained results are compared.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of CUK converter with beta (B) MPPT for standalone PV system
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and simulation of CUK converter with beta MPPT for standalone photovoltaic system.Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controllers are used in PV system to track the maximum power due to its poor efficiency.The system is designed in MATLAB/SIMULINK and the simulation results shows the comparative analysis between Perturb & Observe (P&O) and Beta algorithm for extracting the power from Photovoltaic Array(PVA).

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of time delay processes based on FL, FNN & fractional order controllers
abstract: Time-delay usually appears in any practical system like electrical, mechanical, chemical processes and it has a prominent outcome on system operation. This paper introduces an improved design method of different types of intelligent integer type and fractional type PID controllers and their comparison with conventional PID controllers is discussed here to illustrate the superiority of the designed controller for the stable and unstable time delay processes. The performance analysis of different types of controller has been tested by Matlab Simulink and simulation results show that the intelligent type PID and fractional order PID (PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup>) controllers successfully improve the in general performance.

articleTitle: Application of wireless technology in SAIL plants
abstract: Wireless transmission of signals is a futuristic technology, that enables sending and receiving of signals without any physical wires. Control cable connections for equipment in hostile steel plant environment cause breakdowns, with associated productivity loss, due to damage to cables. Further, there are areas where cable laying is extremely difficult. It is also common to encounter signal loss when they are transmitted over long distances. Safety of operating personnel is also sometimes compromised due to close vicinity of flowing hot molten metal. Since modern steel plants are designed to deliver consistent productivity and quality, reliable wireless signal communication systems have to be aggressively developed and incorporated to avoid breakdowns and accidents for augmenting system output and efficiency. Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), with its in house technical capability has developed and implemented wireless signal transmission systems.

articleTitle: Stabilization and tracking of uncertain nonlinear systems with unobservable dynamics and time delay
abstract: This work examines the stabilization and output tracking of a class of nonlinear systems in the presence of parametric uncertainty, unobservable dynamics and time delay. The proposed method minimizes the tracking error and guarantees delay independent stabilization by means of a modified input-output linearization method, which in turn is modelled using the Mean Value Theorem approach. Also a comparison is made herewith a previous method [1] through the same design example to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Steady state harmonic stability analysis in IEEE 14 bus system for fault at generator bus
abstract: In this paper steady state harmonic stability has been assessed in IEEE 14 bus system for fault at generator bus. It has been achieved by applying passivity based impedance model in Gauss-Seidal iteration technique. Power and load angle have been determined at normal condition as well during fault condition at generator bus. Fundamental and harmonic bus voltages have been determined both for normal and fault conditions. Operating points in P-δ plane have been identified and zone of operation has been assessed for both fundamental and harmonic components. Significant shift of the harmonic operating points have been observed during fault condition.

articleTitle: Construction of extended das and Ghoshal observer for a class of nonlinear systems
abstract: This paper presents the formulation of a reduced order observer for a class of non-linear systems based on generalized matrix inverse. The class of nonlinear system considers, the system dynamics being nonlinear with linear output relation. The state vector is decomposed into two orthogonal components, having the known component is along the system output and the orthogonal component being unknown. The estimation of the unknown component essentially leads to reconstruction of full state information. Illustrative numerical examples with simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of capacitor in radial distribution systems using oppositional krill herd algorithm
abstract: For supplying reactive power in order to decrease power loss, capacitors equipped distribution systems are used. This paper presents an efficient optimization algorithm named oppositional krill herd (OKH) algorithm for selecting the installation locations of the capacitors to reduce power loss considering different constraints in radial distribution system. To prove the feasibility and superiority of the planned OKH algorithm, 34-bus and 69-bus radial distribution systems are used as test studies and the obtained results are compared with other reported methods. Comparison study with other reported method demonstrate the fact that the proposed method gains upper hand in solving optimum capacitor planning problem in radial distribution system.

articleTitle: EEG complex grasping patterns recognition for BMI robotic and prosthesis motion control
abstract: Capturing features of brainwaves (Electroencephalographic EEG activity), and brain patterns involved in grasping is not a trivial task. This is due to the complication of such patterns. In this context, this paper will be focusing on mechanisms of decoding and learned patterns of neural waves for robotic grasping applications. This is based on using c-mean clustering routines, as associated with PCA for dimensionality reduction. The learned waves features and patterns, are hence use with MBI for motorizing and controlling a Robotic-prosthesis, or even for rehabilitation applications. The paper will be focusing on dealing with massive interrelated waves features, and how PCA learning patterns are used for motorizing and motion applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of Q- and X-MRAS for speed sensor less induction motor drive on
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study between a wellknown instantaneous reactive power (Q) based MRAS (QMRAS) and a relatively new X-MRAS used for sensorless speed estimation of induction motor drive from the stability point of view. The instantaneous and steady state values of Q are considered to develop the reference and adaptive models respectively for the former whereas those of a G fictitious quantity X (i.e., v⃗*×i̅) are considered in the said models for the later. Non computation of flux in these schemes makes the speed estimation possible over a wide speed range maintaining the drive's stability in all the 4-quadrants. Moreover, Q-/X-MRAS are dependent on rotor resistance variation whereas X-MRAS is also influenced by the stator resistance variation. A small signal stability analysis over a wide range of stator and rotor resistance variations is carried out to ensure the drive's stability for both MRASs. Matlab/Simulink is used to carry out the proposed study and results are being validated in a prototype experimental setup using dSPACE 1104 controller.

articleTitle: Track following control of hard disc drive: A survey
abstract: The head-positioning accuracy of the hard disc drive should be less than 10% of the track width to ensure that the user data on the adjacent track is not erased during writing. For that purpose the track-following controllers are used to minimize the value of Position Error Signal (PES) as small as possible for both the nominal and perturbed plants in the presence of disturbances & noise. A comparative study is done on different controllers (classical, robust & optimal) in this thesis to compare the efficiency of improving the performance of the track following control of HDD.

articleTitle: A robust slip based traction control of electric vehicle under different road conditions
abstract: This Paper focuses on controlling the value of Longitudinal Slip ratio using sliding mode control method for electric vehicles at different road conditions from the standpoint of stability and improving the performance. In this process sliding mode control is used to ensure robustness from the model parameter uncertainties and a control law is proposed based on Lyapunov stability theory to guarantee the sliding condition. By setting optimal slip value at a limit we can assure that at that point maximum driving force available by maximizing tire-road friction force. MATLAB/SIMULINK environment Simulation assessments support the demonstration of the effectiveness of proposed method as it is tested on varying parameter.

articleTitle: Open loop speed control of a space vector PWM Inverter fed PM synchronous motor
abstract: In this work a simple low-cost open-loop speed control technique has been developed for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) without damper winding. The problem with rotor position sensor-less open-loop control of PMSM without damper winding is its inherent instability at higher speed. It is identified in this work that the rate of change of motor terminal frequency and voltage are the two key factors which affect the stability and dynamic performance of the motor. The values of rate of change of frequency and voltage are determined experimentally for optimal performance of the motor. The space vector pulse width modulated (SVPWM) voltage source Inverter (VSI) is used to generate the variable frequency and variable voltage supply with minimum amount of harmonic distortion. A new algorithm has been developed to implement the control scheme using a 8-bit microcontroller instead of DSP, FPGA or high performance 16-bit microcontroller to reduce the cost and complexity of the drive. Satisfactory performance of the proposed technique has been demonstrated using a developed hardware prototype in real time.

articleTitle: Effect of intrinsic layer on the performance of InGaP/GaAs dual Junction solar cell
abstract: In this paper, the effect of an intrinsic layer inside the PN junction of both top and bottom cell of InGaP/GaAs Double Junction solar cell is investigated using computational TCAD modeling tool. Inclusion of intrinsic layer shows better performance in comparison to other structures and produces high conversion efficiency of 29.72% (1sun), high shortcircuit current density and open circuit voltage. For this optimized cell structure, the maximum J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</sub>=13.65mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</sub>=2.44 V, fill factor (FF) = 89.08 are obtained under AM1.5G illumination. The detail of photo-generation rate of top as well as bottom cell has been investigated through the incident light of various wavelengths.

articleTitle: Oppositional cuckoo optimization algorithm for optimal tuning of power system stabilizers
abstract: In this novel approach, oppositional based learning is implemented on cuckoo optimization algorithm to tune the power system stabilizer parameters which are added to the excitation system to damp low frequency oscillation that pertain in large power system. Eigen value based objective function incorporating damping factor and damping ratio of lightly damped electromechanical modes is considered in the PSSs design problem. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated on a single machine infinite bus from the Heffron-Phillips model. The most important advantage of applying oppositional based cuckoo optimization algorithm is that it quickly reaches to the optimal solution. From the computational results, it is revealed that the proposed algorithm gains upper hand in damping the low frequency oscillations. Results are presented over a wide range of loading condition to show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. Simulated results of the proposed OCOA method are compared with those obtained by COA, OGSA, GSA and DE to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Content summarization using video decomposition
abstract: With the increasing usage of visual media, it is becoming difficult to store, search and manage them properly due to their large data size. Sorting a video manually is a tedious work and does not produce efficient results. Thus it is becoming absolutely necessary to invent modern techniques that can minimize the effort of the user by summarizing the content of a video in an effective way such that any user can interpret the actual flow of incident in the video instantaneously. Unfortunately development of such algorithm is not straight forward due to several reasons like large number of frames, frame resolution, motion etc. Estimation of a single image containing the event happening in a video is the fastest and most intuitive way to represent the entire video. In this paper we propose a novel method to summarize the content of a video using total variation based video decomposition.

articleTitle: A comparative study on gene ranking and classification methods using microarray gene expression profiles
abstract: Microarray gene expression profiles are generally consists of very large number of genes. The total numbers of samples in the gene expression profiles are usually very less. Therefore, ranking of informative genes plays an important role in sample classification. In this paper, we present a comparative study on different gene ranking methods by applying them to two datasets. Support vector machine (SVM) with different kernels and a K-nearest neighbor (K-NN) classifier have been used to perform the classification task. Our results demonstrate the importance of informative gene ranking to classify test samples accurately.

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation of Dual Metal Double Gate SON MOSFET using hafnium dioxide for better performance
abstract: Advancement of semiconductor device in sub 45 nm range has led to lots of development in device area, but it also raises some critical issues. One of such an issues is related to silicon dioxide layer which starts breakdown once its thickness is around 2nm range due to gate leakage current. In this paper, we try to overcome this problem by replacing the front gate silicon dioxide dielectric layer of dual material double gate silicon on nothing MOSFET by high k dielectric material layer, hafnium dioxide. This paper gives an analysis of the important parameter of semiconductor device such as threshold voltage and surface potential changes with change of dielectric layer to Hafnium dioxide from conventional silicon dioxide. The results are validated in ATLAS 2D simulation tools.

articleTitle: Analytical computation of stored charge inside real MOS structure for power device applications
abstract: Dependence of stored charge on surface potential and gate voltage is analytically computed for real MOS capacitor. `Real'ness is taken into account by considering carrier concentration as a function of both surface potential and Fermi level at equilibrium condition, where the incorporation of Fermi level significantly affects the electrical performance of the structure. Variation of stored charge is computed by varying structural parameters within appreciable practical limit, doping concentration and flatband voltage. Simulation reveals that suitable choice of external bias and structural parameters are essential for designing the device in high power applications.

articleTitle: Low voltage DC microgrid-overview for reduction in substantial losses
abstract: In today's world renewable energy sources (like PV, wind etc) has become one of the most promising sources of energy for power generation because of its positive effect on environment. Tomorrow's distributed renewable generation and today's electronic equipment requires us to rethink on the current AC model. The increasing prevalence for DC appliances in the technologically advanced society is attracting the concept of DC micro-grid. In case of various renewable resources (like the rooftop solar) produces DC in that case DC-AC-DC conversion has to be made hence resulting in substantial loss of energy. In this paper, an overview of possible solution to this energy loss problem is given, in order to improve the efficiency and reliability of the implementation of micro grid.

articleTitle: Comparative study of dielectric response functions for characterizing time domain polarization process in transformer insulation
abstract: Analysis of dielectric response measurements has been a topic of great interest to power engineers in recent times. Time domain polarization measurements are one of the most popular dielectric testing techniques for condition assessment of transformer's insulation. For accurate interpretation of test data various mathematical models of the dielectric response process have been proposed by various researchers over the years. Many of these models are based on the basis dielectric physics and some are based on circuit models. The mathematical function most commonly used to represent dielectric test data is the so called “dielectric response function”. The present contribution makes an attempt to compare the suitability of different mathematical formulations of the dielectric response function for describing the test data. Experimental results on laboratory scaled down models and also on real transformers have been presented to support the theoretical formulations.

articleTitle: A new approach of controlled binning for data smoothening
abstract: Binning is a process of noise removal from data. It is an important step of preprocessing where data smoothening occurs by computation of the data points. The knowledge which is to be extracted from the data is very crucial which demands for a control in the loss of data. We have developed a method by which the user can control the level of data smoothening by binning. The acceptable loss percentage on individual data points is asked from the user. Allowable loss is calculated and a decision is made to smoothen the value or retain it .Our proposed method will let the user get a requirement based output. Our proposed algorithm will allow the user to interact with the data preprocessing system unlike the older algorithms. Different stages of smoothened outputs are obtained by different loss percentages. This preprocessed output produced will be of a better quality and will resemble more to the real world data.

articleTitle: Frequency deviation control of a thermal and hydro area connected system
abstract: Maintaining system frequency within the acceptable tolerance is always a crucial aspect of multi-area power systems. This paper presents a load frequency control (LFC) design of a thermal and hydro connected power system. Performance of a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller is investigated in the proposed LFC. Bacterial Foraging algorithm is used for optimization of controller parameters. MATLAB based simulation shows that the controller maintains frequency deviation within the acceptable limit under load variations.

articleTitle: Simulation of a proposed PV based microgrid for a hostel building in Thapar University
abstract: This paper presents the concept of microgrid and a sample case study for proposed PV based microgrid, to secure the load demands of an university hostel building. The proposed system is modeled in Matlab-Simulink software (SimPower) based on real data of the site and the simulation results are found satisfactory at this preliminary level of planning and design which would prove useful, prior to future on-site installation. The proposed microgrid model is able to show satisfactory behavior while operating in grid connected as well as islanded mode and feed the load demands of hostel.

articleTitle: A new neighborhood connectivity based clustering approach for energy reduction in mobile networks
abstract: The energy content in a network mainly depends on the number of clusters and cluster heads. Hence the clustering procedure is very significant towards efficient network resource utilization. The transmission range and layout of the nodes play a very important role in any clustering methodologies. In this paper, a new clustering approach involving transmission range, location of a node in the network and neighborhood awareness of each nodeis introduced. This proposed method identifies potential cluster heads and performs clustering using the connectivity information of the node. It is compared with other existing approaches and analyzed to attain superiority over them.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-PSO approach for control in nonlinear systems - real time application
abstract: Nonlinear problems are very common in many industrial applications. For controlling such systems there are several conventional type of controllers intended , such as manual controller, P, PI, PID, and fuzzy controllers. In recent decade new family of intelligent controllers has been evolved because of vary complicated systems and due to requirement of accuracy in the process. The paper consists of Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy controller designed for nonlinear system with time delay and optimized fuzzy controller in which particle swarm optimization is used to optimize the fuzzy rules. Here in this paper the CSTR model is considered to design a fuzzy controller. At the end, simulation results are given to show the effectiveness of system with optimized fuzzy controller.

articleTitle: Order reduction of uncertain systems using the advantages of two varied approximations
abstract: Transfer function of higher orders from physical system makes the overall study and analysis uneasy demanding an approximate model that preserves the basic characteristics of the original model. Also, rigorous study and analysis of physical system lead to the outcome of systems with uncertainty instead of certain coefficients. Thus, systems having uncertain but bounded parameters known as uncertain systems are under consideration in this paper. As a whole, an effective algorithm to determine the reduced order model is proposed here. This methodology is verified using numerical examples available from the literatures and compared with other method.

articleTitle: Novel control strategy of static Kramer induction generator
abstract: This paper presents the mathematical models of static Kramer induction generator (SKIG) that greatly improves its performance to be competitor for wind energy and hydraulic power generation. First, the effect of imposing negative voltage vector to the rotor at super synchronous speed is examined. Statorflux orientation (SFO) at rotor unity power factor (UPF) mathematical model is presented. Two models of control strategies are proposed, the first is to control the imposed rotor voltage, thus an angular relationship between stator voltage and rotor voltage vectors over the operating speed range is established, which may be achieved by regulating the slip of the machine through the grid side converter (GSC) to fix the operating technique. The second one is to control the rotor current via GSC. GSC is a PWM Voltage Source Converter. A comparison between the two techniques is given and very good matching is obtained. Both control strategies can be achieved in terms of the GSC firing angle. In addition to the greatly improved power factor, the paper illustrates the availability of extending the operating speed range up to twice of the synchronous speed, however, the speed range must be limited by GSC ratings to achieve the slip recovery advantage of lowering the interfacing grid converter rating .In analogy the system may be applied for electric drives as well.

articleTitle: Optimal design of a hybrid power system using a new improved particle swarm optimization technique
abstract: Wind - Photovoltaic Hybrid System utilization is becoming popular day by day given to its reliable energy resources, decreasing prices of turbines and PV panels and increase in overall energy cost and reduced emission. Design and scheduling of such a hybrid system can be done using various techniques like genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization, etc. One of the major difficulties in these methods is the premature convergence. This paper presents a new improved particle swarm optimization technique to avoid premature convergence while optimizing the overall cost of energy of a hybrid power system. The system under consideration consists of a wind turbine, a Photovoltaic Generator, a diesel generator and a battery bank. The results obtained by the proposed method are compared with an iterative method. It is found that the proposed method can produce superior results.

articleTitle: A wavelet based novel method for identification of harmonics in a signal
abstract: Presence of harmonics in power system is a major concern in power system due to extensive use of power electronic devices. It is a necessary requirement that the specific harmonics be identified so that corrective measures can be taken. This paper presents a new method for identifying the presence of specific harmonic levels in voltage signal based on discrete wavelet transform. The detail voltage at the first level of decomposition is considered for analysis. Identification of harmonics is done by using different sampling frequencies so that contribution of each harmonics can be clearly estimated. The simulation results presented here show that the proposed method can effectively indicate the presence of specific harmonics levels in a signal.

articleTitle: Analytical study and overview on glove based Indian Sign Language interpretation technique
abstract: This research presents the development issue with proper information of several current improvements on gloves base sing language interpreter. Through this paper a specific comparative approach is implemented towards the sensor selection for gloves based sign language technology. Paper mainly contributes the implementation technique of accelerometer, flex sensor and gyroscopic action towards better efficacy of gloves. Parametric study is added for several sensors with critical comparative approach in consideration of proposed gloves prototype model. Socially, this research study is carrying it's important for betterment of deaf-mute people.

articleTitle: Nonlinear phenomena in permanent magnet Brushless DC motor drive
abstract: Studies of nonlinear phenomena have been made for Brushless DC (BLDC) motor. The operations in periodic region like period-1, period-2 or high periodic along with operation in chaotic region due to variation of different parameters like controller gain, load torque, reference speed etc. have been reported. This study helps to select the operating parameters of the BLDC drive to achieve quality performance.

articleTitle: HBBO optimization for optimal reactive power dispatch incorporating TCSC and TCPS devices
abstract: This paper proposes a new hybrid biogeography based optimization (HBBO) approach for solving complex optimal reactive power dispatch (ORPD) problem in order to improve voltage profile and network losses. Flexible AC transmission system (FACTS) has become commonly used device to improve the laudability and overall performance of power system and can also maintain the power system to run under normal conditions. Here, two types of FACTS devices namely, thyristor-controlled series capacitor (TCSC) and thyristor-controlled phase shifter (TCPS) are considered for minimizing voltage deviation and transmission loss. The efficiency and accuracy of the proposed approach is demonstrated on a standard IEEE 30-bus test system. In this study, the optimization results obtained from HBBO are analyzed and compared with the same obtained by artificial bee colony (ABC), particle swarm optimization with inertia weight approach (PSOIWA) and real-coded genetic algorithm (RGA). A comparison of simulation results reveals optimization efficacy of the proposed scheme over other approaches.

articleTitle: Content
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: control system; power system; instrumentation and measurement; power electronics; and energy.
